FORESKIN
Just the tip (of what’s to come)

It started, as the best ideas do, over drinks — when one of us complained about a delivery gone missing (“I’ve been waiting on this package all week”) and the whole table heard something else entirely. The word never recovered. Neither did we.

What follows is a study in fabric. The same subject matter, again and again, framed by denim, by cotton, by the occasional questionable spandex. A catalog. Everything one of a kind, nothing for sale. Probably.

Nobody warned us it would become an obsession — least of all for the lesbians, mothers, and grandmothers now studying packages with the focus of art historians and the discretion of none.

So if you’re a fellow package watcher: welcome. You’ve found your people.

— Anita P. Book
Dedication
For everyone who has ever
pretended not to look.

Appendicks
Glossary
A working vocabulary
Package watcher, n.One who notices, appreciates, and quietly files it away for later. You. Us. Everyone, if pressed.
Packtivity, n.A subject’s activity of choice; also, a socially acceptable reason to keep looking.
Grower / ShowerA distinction of enormous personal significance and no scientific value whatsoever.
VolumeThe loudness at which a package announces itself upon arrival. Ranges from quiet to loud.
ForeskinSee: the foreword. Uncut and unabridged.
Book, Anita P.Your author. The “P.” is for Package. Probably. Possibly. Persistently. (What did you think it stood for?)
Appendicks
Handling Key
Reading the labels
📦Handle with care — treat gently; worth the trouble.
⬆️This end up — you’ll know it when you see it.
⚠️Fragile — approach with the appropriate respect.
✍️Signature required — you’ll want proof you were here.
❄️Perishable — best enjoyed fresh.
